findings.title: Header values above U+00FF pass validation and the SPI does not pin the header encoding
findings.description: isFieldValue only rejects C0 controls and DEL. Any char above 0x7F passes, including chars above 0xFF such as U+010A or U+010D. HttpExchange.commit takes headers as Java Strings and does not say how the adapter turns them into bytes. An adapter that writes headers as ISO-8859-1 by keeping the low byte (the classic char-to-byte cast, the cause of Node.js header-splitting CVE-2018-12116) turns U+010A into LF and U+010D into CR, which gets past the CR/LF guard the A-003 fix was meant to provide. The core is the trust boundary here and the SPI leaves the encoding open.
findings.suggested_fix: Either reject chars > 0xFF in isFieldValue (RFC 9110 allows only obs-text 0x80-0xFF), or state in HttpExchange.commit javadoc how header strings become bytes (for example ISO-8859-1, with chars > 0xFF never reaching the adapter). Add a test case {"X", "a\u010Ab"} next to the existing bad-header table.

findings.title: The in-memory adapter still does not catch a short body or a header/argument length mismatch
findings.description: B-001 is resolved: the length is recorded, exposed, asserted in the tests, and an over-long write fails. Two parts of the suggested fix were not done. (1) finish() does not mark the exchange abnormal when fewer than contentLength bytes were written, so a regression that commits N and writes less would still pass. (2) commit() counts Content-Length headers (more than one fails) but does not check that a single header equals contentLength on a non-HEAD response, which is the rule the new HttpExchange.commit javadoc sets.
findings.suggested_fix: In finish(), when contentLength >= 0 and body.size() < contentLength, mark the exchange aborted or throw IOException. Optionally, when the request method is not HEAD and a Content-Length header is present, require it to equal contentLength.
